transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-19
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya & Marco (Redwood SEs), Jordan, Maya, Samir, Leah, Tina (Catalyst)

Summary (auto):
Short kickoff to align on pilot milestones, what access Catalyst needs to provide, and what Redwood will deliver (benchmarks, runbook, pricing). Discussed success criteria including latency P99, cost per 1k tokens target, embedding recall thresholds, and data controls (S3/KMS).

00:00 Speaker 1 (Alex): hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick round robin names then jump into the roadmap for the pilot, um we want to keep this tight so we can get to the midpoint review with meaningful numbers
00:22 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Jordan here — head of ml at catalyst labs. Thanks for setting this up. We're excited but we have some compliance slotted into the decision — so we'll need clear gates
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): Priya from Redwood, i'll be leading the benchmark and ops side, hello all
00:42 Speaker 4 (Maya): maya from infra / sres. i'll own access and infra tickets. quick note we have separate prod and research aws accounts
00:50 Speaker 1 (Alex): great, thanks — agenda is: kickoff + timeline, success criteria, workload sizing, access & security, then milestones and next steps

05:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): to start success criteria — what would you consid-er a pass at midpoint and at exec readout? we usually split into: functional quality, latency/throughput, and cost economics
05:29 Speaker 2 (Jordan): good call. functional quality: we need embeddings recall > 0.85 on our held out set for top-5 retrieval; generation quality judged by product at a 4/5 threshold on our prompt rubric. latency: p99 under 400ms for 1k token responses, target p50 < 120ms. cost: ideally under $0.15 per 1k tokens (including cache savings).
05:55 Speaker 5 (Samir): and to add we need a spike resilience test — our traffic can burst 5x during daytime peaks so throughput must sustain that without > 15% error rate
06:14 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok noted. we'll design benchmark phases: baseline (hosted default settings), optimized (batching + cache + quantization where appropriate), and stress (burst 5x). each phase has pass/fail metrics

11:03 Speaker 4 (Maya): access questions — we will need an architectural play: do you need cross-account role? we'll want to control S3 and KMS. we also have sensitive customer PII in some datasets so encryption & retention matter
11:21 Speaker 1 (Alex): yes we typically ask for an S3 bucket and an IAM role ARN for Redwood to pull test data, or we can run a private deployment if you prefer data stays in your VPC. which direction are you leaning?
11:35 Speaker 6 (Tina): security here — SOC2 ok, but if we push any production data into hosted we need a contract amendment; our preference is to start with redacted / synthetic data and then evaluate a private flow for the exec phase if needed
11:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): makes sense. for the pilot we can accept synthetic/derisked data for initial benchmarks. we'll include a privacy runbook and we can demo a private deployment checklist if you choose that route later

17:40 Speaker 3 (Priya): workload sizing — can you share typical request / day and mean tokens per request? that helps us size reserved capacity if you go dedicated or estimate costs for hosted
17:54 Speaker 2 (Jordan): today the research team sends ~70k requests/day at 300 tokens avg, but product sim shows production ramp to ~300k requests/day over 6 months. 95th percentile sequence length is 800 tokens during long reads
18:18 Speaker 5 (Samir): also note embedding generation for search runs nightly on batches totalling ~10M tokens/day — so throughput for embeddings is critical too
18:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok so pilot workload we should model: 1) interactive generation baseline 70k/day -> scale to 300k/day, 2) embeddings nightly 10M tokens/day, 3) peak bursts 5x. we'll propose concurrency & GPU sizing accordingly

23:05 Speaker 1 (Alex): timeline and milestones — here's the proposed 6 week pilot runway:
- Week 0 (kickoff): Access setup, send benchmark template, confirm success criteria
- Week 1: Baseline runs (hosted) with synthetic data; collect latency + quality
- Week 2-3: Optimization phase (batching, caching, quantized weights where feasible), iterate on prompts
- Week 4: Stress & scale tests, embeddings throughput test at night window
- Week 5: Midpoint review with execs for preliminary readout; decide hosted vs private for exec phase based on gates
- Week 6: Final readout & handoff; produce runbook and ops playbook
23:40 Speaker 4 (Maya): that sounds workable; what happens if mid-point fails a gate? what's your fallback policy?
23:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): our standard gates: if latency or quality are >20% off targets, we do a targeted remediation sprint (2 weeks) and re-evaluate. if security or data controls are insufficient we pause hosted and shift to a private deployment plan — that's a heavier lift and has separate timelines

30:12 Speaker 6 (Tina): can you spell out what we need to provide for the hosted benchmark vs the private benchmark?
30:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes. For hosted: synthetic data files on your S3 (or we can generate), IAM cross-account role ARN, list of IPs for allowlist if needed, and minimal compliance docs. For private: access to a bastion or VPC peering details, KMS key material handshake, and an infra contact for on-prem package install windows

35:10 Speaker 1 (Alex): pricing conversation briefly — we will email a pilot quote. it will include expected GPU hours for the optimization phase, and a separate estimate for Dedicated vs Private setup. note: dedicated pools have a setup lead time of about 3-4 weeks
35:35 Speaker 5 (Samir): budget constraints are real — if hosted is cheaper we'll default there but we need guardrails to avoid data leakage. also curious about automatic fallback if capacity is constrained, how does Redwood route?
35:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): smart routing: we can route by latency window or by region and have automated fallback to a cheaper model variant. for the pilot we'll instrument that and show cost/latency tradeoffs in the dashboard

41:00 Speaker 4 (Maya): benchmarks — what exact metrics will you deliver? and in what format?
41:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): we'll deliver a benchmark spreadsheet with: per-model p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, embedding recall/precision on your gold set, error rates under burst. we'll also provide raw logs and a small dashboard snapshot. template will be shared as a Google Sheet link

47:28 Speaker 2 (Jordan): ok for quality checks we want a blind eval: sample outputs mixed with current baseline and annotate the preferability. can you run blind evals?
47:40 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes we'll support blind A/B evaluations and we'll include instructions so your product team can do the annotation and we can aggregate a score for the exec readout

52:15 Speaker 1 (Alex): decision gates recap — what are the pass criteria for the exec readout? Priya you want to say them?
52:26 Speaker 3 (Priya): sure. Exec readout pass =
- Quality: >= 0.85 embedding recall (top-5) and generation preferability >= 4/5 per your rubric
- Latency: p99 <= 400ms for interactive flows at target concurrency, embeddings throughput >= 10M tokens/day without degradation
- Cost: projected steady-state cost within 20% of your target ($0.15 per 1k tokens)
- Security: access & retention controls verified (S3/KMS) or private deployment plan approved
52:58 Speaker 6 (Tina): and legal needs to sign an addendum before any real customer PII moves to hosted, noted

58:09 Speaker 1 (Alex): ok final run through of next steps and owners — Alex will send pricing and resourcing, Priya sends benchmark harness and shared sheet, Maya opens access ticket and gives role ARNs, Samir to confirm hosted vs private decision window. we'll schedule a midpoint for the week of 2026-06-22.
58:45 Speaker 2 (Jordan): sounds good — thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity
58:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): thanks all, we'll follow up with the sheet and an access checklist
59:05 Speaker 1 (Alex): end call, thanks

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mislabeling of speaker ids, uh filler words and short overlaps. proper nouns like KMS and VPC sometimes transcribed as kms/vpc or 'k m s' in the raw export, cleaned lightly here.
